title: Joins: Visual Guide
outline: 1. The Product Grid | the 3x3 Cartesian product of users and orders with every ON comparison shown as TRUE, FALSE or UNKNOWN, and a switch that makes one foreign key NULL | a join is pair-everything-then-keep-only-TRUE, so a NULL join key matches nothing ever, and output size is the number of matching pairs

2. Four Ways To Keep | the same two tables under INNER, LEFT, RIGHT and FULL, with padded NULL cells marked | join types differ only in which unmatched rows survive padded with NULL, and FULL JOIN is the reconciliation shape

3. Where The LEFT Dies | the predicate o.amount > 100 moved between ON, WHERE, and WHERE with OR IS NULL, tracked through the join and the filter | ON decides what counts as a match, WHERE deletes rows after the join, so a predicate on the nullable side in WHERE turns a LEFT JOIN into an inner join

4. Grain Keeper | six ways to ask does-a-match-exist, with row count and output grain, plus a switch that puts one NULL in orders.user_id | EXISTS and NOT EXISTS keep the left grain without DISTINCT, and NOT IN against a nullable column silently returns zero rows

5. Fan-out Multiplier | sliders for one user's order count and login count, showing m x n emitted rows and the inflated SUM(amount) against the true one | joining two one-to-many tables multiplies both sides, inflating totals by a factor that differs per key, and the cure is to aggregate to the target grain before joining
